text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Defence Minister Jan Sitek said central European countries could become a buffer zone if there is a deterioration of relations between Russia and the West.
- Sitek said the Slovak army would be fully NATO-compatible by the end of 1999.

- Peter Mihok, chairman of the Slovak Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said that exclusion of Slovakia from the first wave of post-communist coutries accepted to the European Union would have catastrophic consequencies for the economy and the social standards of its citizens.

- Jan Carnogursky, leader of the opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), said the revised version of the controversial law on protection of the republic, worked out by deputies of the ruling coalition, was unacceptable as it still allowed punishment for expressing opinions and may limit freedom of information.

SME - The legislative council of the Slovak government on Thursday approved the revised version of the law on protection of the republic. The draft law will now be discussed by the government and is expected to be presented to parliament at its next session, starting December 4.
PRAVDA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar he would prefer a referendum on the integration to NATO and European Union (EU) to be held in May 1997.

- Meciar said Slovakia still had to chose from several alternatives for integration into Western structures -- membership both in NATO and EU, membership only in one of these organisations, or staying neutral from both organisations.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, aproved another 55 privatisation decisions. The sales totalled 915 million crowns.
- Agriculture Minister Peter Baco said the government was preparing a special bank to support small and medium-sized enterprises.
- Slovakia's largest cellulose and paper producer SCP Ruzomberok said it planned to invest about 1.5 billion crowns in ecological projects in the near future.
- The Czech-based bank Banka Hana opened in its eighth Slovak office in Bratislava.
